description: Per-formula integrity check (Step 6): numerator, denominator, edge-case behaviour, and whether this phase changed anything. Verified against source; every 'unchanged' means byte-identical to the pre-Phase-9.1 code.

formulas.zero_denominator: if total_demand == 0: returns 1.0 (an if/else convention — NOT max(total_demand, 1e-6) as the pre-existing audit claimed)
formulas.missing_input: not applicable — always computable from a solved NetworkStateResult
formulas.negative_input: not applicable — both inputs are non-negative by construction (MILP demand/flow are >= 0)
formulas.infeasible_result: compute_kpis zero-fills the ENTIRE NetworkKPIs (a pre-existing, verified, tested behaviour). The KPI layer does NOT repeat this: KPIRegistry.network_kpis reads NetworkStateResult.solver_status/is_feasible FIRST and reports KPIStatus.INFEASIBLE with value=None, rather than trusting the engine's own zero-fill as a measurement.
formulas.empty_dataset: a network with zero demand records yields total_demand=0, handled by the same zero-denominator convention above
formulas.partial_dataset: not applicable — fill rate is computed once per solve, not incrementally
formulas.wrong_unit: verified: a FRACTION [0,1], never multiplied by 100 anywhere in the KPI layer
formulas.wrong_scope: NETWORK only — no per-facility or per-market fill rate exists in the codebase today

formulas.zero_denominator: if not is_open or capacity_units <= 0: returns 0.0 (verified, milp.py:677-678)
formulas.negative_input: not possible by construction — capacity and flow are both >= 0
formulas.infeasible_result: same INFEASIBLE handling as FILL_RATE (network-level); per-facility utilization on an infeasible solve is not produced at all (facility_kpis returns {} when no NetworkStateResult exists)
formulas.empty_dataset: a network with zero facilities yields an empty facility_kpis dict, never a fabricated entry
formulas.wrong_scope: both NETWORK (avg/max/min) and FACILITY (per-facility) exist as distinct metric_ids in this phase's contract

formulas.zero_denominator: if max(economic_impact) == 0 for every facility: normalize_rei returns REI=0 for all, REIStatus.NO_RELATIVE_COST_EXPOSURE, explicitly 'no division is performed' (rei.py:480-487) — verified NOT a silent 0/0
formulas.missing_input: if PI_i is None (infeasible/error): rei stays None, calculation_status reflects why (INFEASIBLE/ERROR/TIME_LIMIT) — the KPI layer reports NOT_COMPUTABLE with that reason, never fabricating a 0
formulas.negative_input: a negative PI (disruption REDUCES cost) is retained and diagnosed, never silently clamped at the PI level; only the REI-feeding economic_impact is floored to 0
formulas.infeasible_result: calculation_status=INFEASIBLE, rei stays None, risk_classification=CRITICAL (if infeasible_is_critical, the default) — verified end-to-end via a real infeasible-disruption test case in the resilience test suite
formulas.empty_dataset: NoEligibleFacilitiesError is raised (rei.py:1006-1013) when no facility qualifies — the KPI layer's resilience_kpis reports INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE rather than an empty success
formulas.partial_dataset: a batch with some facilities OK and some ERROR/INFEASIBLE reports REIBatchStatus.COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS; each row is wrapped independently, so an ERROR row's rei is NOT_COMPUTABLE while OK rows remain VALID

formulas.zero_denominator: not applicable — no division in this formula
formulas.missing_input: if either P or REI is None: RFStatus.NOT_COMPUTABLE with a specific RFNotComputableReason (NO_EVENT_PROBABILITY / NO_REI / NO_INPUTS) — verified P is NEVER defaulted to 0.0
formulas.negative_input: P outside [0,1]+-1e-9 raises ValidationFailureError (never silently clamped); REI < -1e-9 is floored to 0 with a note appended (never raises, never silently discarded)
formulas.infeasible_result: not directly applicable to RF itself — if REI is unavailable because its facility's disruption was infeasible, RF reports NOT_COMPUTABLE(NO_REI)
formulas.empty_dataset: assess_network_risk SKIPS (does not zero-default) any facility missing either input — verified via its own docstring and code
formulas.partial_dataset: RiskAssessment.results / .not_computable are two separate lists — a caller sees exactly which facilities computed and which did not, never a merged list with fabricated zeros
formulas.wrong_scope: FACILITY only (network-level max_risk_factor is a simple max() over the facility rows, not a separately-computed formula)

formulas.formula: co2_kg = distance_km * (flow_units * weight_kg / 1000) * emission_factor, summed across flows
formulas.missing_input: missing emission factor falls back to ROAD default (0.062 kg CO2/tonne-km) — a documented, tested fallback, not a silent zero
formulas.negative_input: not possible by construction — flow, weight, distance are all >= 0
formulas.infeasible_result: an infeasible solve has no flows, so total_carbon_kg is 0 by construction (zero flows = zero carbon, a true zero, not a fabricated one) — but the KPI layer still reports INFEASIBLE status per the network-level infeasibility check, since '0 carbon because the network never solved' must not be read as 'a solved network with 0 carbon'
formulas.empty_dataset: zero facilities/flows yields 0.0 by arithmetic, verified by test_carbon.py::test_zero_flow_zero_co2
formulas.partial_dataset: not applicable — carbon is summed once per solve
formulas.wrong_unit: verified: KILOGRAMS, never tonnes/tCO2e — the pre-existing audit's tCO2e claim is wrong (no kg->tonne conversion exists anywhere in the formula)
formulas.wrong_scope: NETWORK (total_carbon_kg) and per-flow (FlowSummary.carbon_kg) both exist; no facility-level carbon aggregate is computed in the codebase today

formulas.zero_denominator: if naive_mae <= 1e-9: mase = None (verified, validation.py) — never a fabricated ratio
formulas.missing_input: insufficient history (< MIN_TRAIN_PERIODS=6) refuses the backtest entirely; SeriesForecast.accuracy stays None and the KPI layer reports NOT_COMPUTABLE
formulas.negative_input: not applicable — demand quantities are validated non-negative upstream (forecasting/service.py rejects negative demand)
formulas.infeasible_result: not applicable to forecasting (no solver infeasibility concept here)
formulas.empty_dataset: zero-history series never reach backtest; ForecastStatus.INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY is reported instead
formulas.partial_dataset: each series in a multi-series ForecastResult is scored independently; one series' MASE=None never affects another's
formulas.wrong_unit: verified: a dimensionless ratio (MASE < 1.0 beats the naive benchmark)

formulas.formula: sum of included cost components per ResilienceCostBasis flags, excluding the shortage penalty by default
formulas.missing_input: not applicable — always computable from a solved NetworkStateResult
formulas.negative_input: not possible by construction — every cost component is >= 0
formulas.infeasible_result: same network-level INFEASIBLE handling as FILL_RATE
formulas.empty_dataset: a network with no facilities/flows yields business_network_cost=0 by arithmetic (a true zero from an empty sum, not fabricated)

formulas.zero_denominator: if |baseline_value| <= 1e-9: pct_delta = None, reason='baseline is zero, so no percentage change is defined' — mirrors the exact convention orchestrator/twin/service.py::_kpi_deltas already uses
formulas.missing_input: if either side's NetworkStateResult is absent: direction=NOT_COMPARABLE, reason names which side is missing — never a fabricated delta
formulas.negative_input: a negative delta (scenario lower than baseline) is a valid, expected DECREASED direction — not an error
formulas.infeasible_result: an infeasible baseline or scenario means that side's NetworkStateResult still exists (with is_feasible=False) but its cost/fill-rate fields may be pre-zeroed by compute_kpis (see FILL_RATE note) — the delta function does not special-case this today, a documented limitation (see report.md limitations)
formulas.empty_dataset: not applicable at the delta level — handled at the underlying NetworkStateResult level
formulas.partial_dataset: not applicable — each metric's delta is independent
formulas.wrong_unit: the delta's unit matches the underlying metric's unit; percentage deltas are always '%' regardless of the base metric's own unit
formulas.wrong_scope: SCENARIO_COMPARISON, a distinct MetricScope from NETWORK/FACILITY
formulas.phase_9_1_note: NEW arithmetic, but not a new formula — a direct application of the pattern orchestrator/twin/service.py::_kpi_deltas already uses, applied here to fields that pattern does not cover (network-state-level fill rate/utilization/carbon/SLA read directly rather than through a twin state).

conclusion: Zero formulas were changed by this phase. The one new calculation (SCENARIO_DELTA_GENERIC) reuses an existing, tested pattern rather than inventing one, and every edge case it introduces (zero baseline, missing side) mirrors a convention already proven correct elsewhere in the codebase.
